chunks: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ali ibn Ja'far al-Jawhari, from Ibrahim ibn Abdillah al-Kufi, from Abu Sa'id Aqisa, who said:
Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) was asked about intellect, so he said: It is suppressing grief and dealing gently with enemies.

key_terms.التجرع: Swallowing, suppressing — here refers to enduring grief without outward expression
key_terms.العقل: Intellect, reason — a core concept in Islamic philosophy denoting the faculty of rational discernment
key_terms.الغصة: Grief, anguish, a lump in the throat — intense emotional pain
key_terms.مداهنة: Gentle dealing, diplomacy, tactful treatment — managing relations with enemies wisely

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Hasan say about the definition of intellect?
ai.summary: Imam al-Hasan al-Mujtaba (peace be upon him) was asked to define intellect ('aql). He gave a profound two-part answer: true intellect is the ability to swallow one's grief (emotional self-control) and to deal diplomatically with one's enemies (strategic restraint). This was narrated by Abu Sa'id Aqisa, a companion of the Imam, reflecting the practical wisdom the second Imam was known for during the politically turbulent period following the end of his caliphate.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Idris narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi Ahmad b. Yahya b. `Imran al-Ash`ari narrated to us from Ahmad b. Abi `Abdillah from `Ali b. Ja`far al-Jawhari from Ibrahim b. `Abdillah al-Kufi from Abi Sa`id `Aqaysa. He said:
Al-Hasan b. `Ali b. Abi Talib (as) was asked about intellect, so he said: It is suppressing grief and speaking gently to enemies.
